voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`), estVoice (s: the predicted voice length, tools/estimate.py; replaced by the real voice once tools/voice.py has run).

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Shakuntala sub-parva (the Sambhava parva's first tale). CHECKED AGAINST CE 1.62.1–14, 1.63.1–26, 1.64.1–42, 1.65.1–17 (GRETIL e-text of the constituted text, lab/ce; star passages and appendix lines are apparatus and were not used; Ganguli (vulgate) only as a reading aid): Janamejaya asks for the Kuru line from the beginning (1.62.2); the founder of the Paurava line, the mighty Duhshanta, lord of the four-cornered earth (1.62.3: `line`; the CE spells the name Duhshanta; we say Dushyanta, the familiar form, and the plaque gives both); he goes to a dense forest with hundreds of horses and elephants and hundreds of warriors (1.63.1–2: `hunt`); he kills deer and beasts in great number (1.63.13–26; shown, not dwelt on); following the deer he enters another forest, alone, hungry and thirsty (1.64.1–2: `deeper`), crosses a waste and comes to another great wood, cool-winded, flowering, loud with birds and bees (1.64.3–14: `lovely`); there, on the bank of the river Malini, a hermitage with sacred fires (1.64.15–18); he means to see the great seer Kanva, of Kashyapa's line (1.64.25); he posts his army at the forest's gate (1.64.26–27) and lays aside the royal insignia, going on with minister and priest (1.64.29: `left`, the turn); he hears the Vedas chanted and thinks himself in Brahma's world (1.64.30–40: `chant`, "in heaven"); he leaves the ministers and goes on alone, does not see the seer, finds the hermitage empty, and calls aloud: who is here? (1.65.1–2: `empty` and the hook); a maiden lovely as Shri, in an ascetic's dress, comes out and welcomes him (1.65.3–6: `came`); he has come to honour Kanva; where has he gone (1.65.8); her answer: my father has gone from the hermitage to fetch fruit; wait a moment (1.65.9: `father`); he asks who she is and whose (1.65.12–13); she says she is held to be Kanva's daughter (1.65.15); he: the holy one is a celibate (urdhvaretas); how are you his daughter (1.65.16–17: the cliffhanger). The speeches are condensed paraphrase. She is not named in the voice (her name is the next episode's payoff). The slaughter of the hunt (1.63) is one line; the catalogue of learned brahmins (1.64.31–37) is one word, "chanting".
structure: As from episode 41 (script/ARC-41-50.md, script/ARC-51-60.md): COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words; the hook style rotates and never repeats the episode before; no episode of this batch opens on fire) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band → the episode stands alone (every name has an identifier in "names", shown as a plaque) → one question closed (loop.answeredBy), the previous one answered by 15 s (loop.prevAnsweredBy) → turn at 40–60 % after a real silence, a second silence where the story allows → one face close-up with a change of emotion → one signature shot → the cliffhanger with the source line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band that dissolves into frame 1. Per line: pal (the colour script: no hue for more than two lines), cam (≥ 4 distinct moves), tr (transitions born from the medium), amb / foley / music (three sound layers; ambLead / ambLag = J- and L-cuts). Gate: tools/gate.mjs.

loop.hookQuestion: Who answers when the king calls into the empty hermitage?
loop.prevQuestion: Who was the hunting king his family's story began with?
loop.openQuestion: How can a celibate sage have a daughter?

strings.recapLine: The king asked for his own family's story, from the beginning.

lines.speaker: dushyanta
lines.note: COLD OPEN (direct speech in medias res; no fire): a man seen from behind, plainly dressed, a bow on his shoulder, stands in the yard of an empty forest hut and calls; only birds answer. A slow push past his shoulder to the dark doorway. The card low.

lines.text: It begins with Dushyanta, a king of Puru's line.
lines.say: It begins with Dushyanta, [p:120] a king of Puru's line.
lines.note: STORY 0 with the unvoiced recap band (top) · NEW LIGHT (seat-ivory): a tilt down a pale palace wall with a painted line of kings to the living king on his throne: young, strong, crowned (plaque: Dushyanta · a king of Puru's line (Duhshanta); small: Puru · founder of the Paurava kings). Answers episode 52's last line by 5 s.

lines.text: One day he rode out to hunt, with hundreds of horses and elephants.
lines.say: One day he rode out to hunt, [p:150] with hundreds of horses [p:60] and elephants.
lines.note: STORY 1 (hunt-emerald): a fast lateral track through green forest: the king's chariot in front, behind it a wall of horses, elephants and spear tips; deer leap ahead; birds burst up.

lines.text: Chasing deer, hungry and thirsty, he rode on into another forest.
lines.say: Chasing deer, [p:100] hungry and thirsty, [p:120] he rode on [p:60] into another forest.
lines.note: STORY 2 · NEW LIGHT (noon-ochre): the chase thins: a dry open waste at noon, the king alone on his chariot, slowing, wiping his brow; far ahead a dark green line of trees. A pull back makes him small.

lines.text: It was cool, flowering, loud with birds. By the river Malini stood the hermitage of the sage Kanva.
lines.say: It was cool, [p:60] flowering, [p:60] loud with birds. [p:300] By the river Malini [p:100] stood the hermitage [p:60] of the sage Kanva.
lines.note: STORY 3 · THE SIGNATURE SHOT · NEW LIGHT (river-jade): a crane up over the tree tops: blossom, birds wheeling, a bright river bending through the wood, and on its bank a cluster of thatched huts with thin columns of smoke (plaques: Malini · a river of the foothills; Kanva · a great sage).

lines.text: He left his army at the forest's edge, and laid aside the signs of a king.
lines.say: He left his army [p:60] at the forest's edge, [p:200] and laid aside [p:60] the signs of a king.
lines.note: STORY 4 · THE TURN (≈ 48 %) after a real silence (hermitage-green): a rack focus from the crown and jewelled sash laid on a folded cloth in the foreground to the king walking away up the path in a plain dhoti, bare-headed, the massed spears of his army small behind him. The word of the turn: GUEST.

lines.text: He walked in among sacred fires and chanting, and felt he stood in heaven.
lines.say: He walked in [p:60] among sacred fires and chanting, [p:200] and felt he stood in heaven.
lines.note: STORY 5 · NEW LIGHT (wedding-turmeric): a slow orbit: rows of seated hermits chanting by small altar fires, flower-strewn seats, deer lying among them; the king passes through, turning to look, hands joined.

lines.text: But the sage's hut was empty. He called out.
lines.say: But the sage's hut was empty. [p:300] He called out.
lines.note: STORY 6 (the hook's place, now from inside): seen through the hut's dark doorway: the king small in the bright yard, looking about, a hand to his mouth. Frame-within-frame.

lines.text: A young woman in a hermit's dress came out, and welcomed him.
lines.say: A young woman [p:60] in a hermit's dress [p:60] came out, [p:200] and welcomed him.
lines.note: STORY 7 (a second real silence before it; answers the hook) · THE CLOSE-UP (meadow-spring): first she steps from the doorway, bark cloth, flowers in her hair, a water jar for his feet; then his face fills the frame: weariness, then wonder (the eyes widen, the mouth softens). She is not named.

lines.speaker: shakuntala
lines.text: "My father has gone to gather fruit. Wait a moment."
lines.say: My father has gone to gather fruit. [p:260] Wait a moment.
lines.note: STORY 8: the two in the yard, three paces apart: she sets a seat of grass for him and steps back, smiling; he sits, looking up at her.

lines.text: Her father? The sage Kanva was a lifelong celibate. Who was she?
lines.say: Her father? [p:300] The sage Kanva [p:60] was a lifelong celibate. [p:300] Who was she?
lines.note: NEXT 1 (the text's own question, 1.65.16–17): the king's puzzled face turned toward her; then the picture he cannot explain: far off by the river, an old sage with a basket of fruit walking home alone; birds circle over the girl's head. The source line (top).
